http_semantics.note: No illegal parameter or malformed body was involved in the primary observation (bodyless POST in documented form). The failing condition is the deployment mode, which is client-observable (GET /cluster reports status=disabled). The recover face surfaces it as 500 'Service internal error', while sibling faces (DELETE /cluster/peer/{id}, create_sharding_key) surface the SAME condition as 400 'Bad request: Distributed mode disabled' — a face-dependent disposition split within one API family.

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: POST /cluster/recover (actix route, src/actix/api/cluster_api.rs:60) -> recover_current_peer handler (auth manage() check) -> dispatcher.toc().request_snapshot() (toc/mod.rs:546) -> get_consensus_proposal_sender() (toc/mod.rs:775) -> consensus_proposal_sender is None in standalone (no consensus started) -> StorageError::service_error("Qdrant is running in standalone mode") -> ServiceError display 'Service internal error: {description}' (errors.rs:21) -> HttpError ResponseError maps ServiceError to 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (src/actix/helpers.rs:247). The handler's actual semantics are ConsensusOperations::RequestSnapshot (a Raft snapshot/restore request), matching the vendored OpenAPI summary 'Tries to recover current peer Raft state.' rather than the contract's older 'removes cluster metadata and restarts as a single-node cluster' prose.
source_grounding.detail: The 500-on-standalone is not an accidental path: maintainers wrote a dedicated gate constructing a condition-specific error message ('Qdrant is running in standalone mode') on exactly this handler's dependency — the op requires a consensus proposal sender, which only exists when distributed mode is enabled; in standalone the op genuinely cannot execute and the source says so explicitly in the response body. Caveats recorded honestly: (a) no code comment or docstring annotates the CHOICE of 500-vs-4xx for this gate, so the intent evidence is the purpose-written error branch itself, not an explicit '// by design' marker; (b) the same standalone precondition on sibling endpoints (remove_peer, sharding-key ops) is gated as 400 BadRequest 'Distributed mode disabled' — the 500 choice on the recover face is unannotated and family-inconsistent, and that inconsistency is recorded as a surviving observation, not explained away; (c) the vendored v1.18.x OpenAPI documents a 4XX error face for this endpoint, which the 500 disposition does not use.
